claims.text: FeCoCrMnNi is a near-equiatomic random HEA with a simple crystal structure.
In the targeted FeCoCrMnNi-like alloys, disorder primarily manifests as force-constant fluctuations rather than large atomic-size or mass disparities.
The proposed framework explicitly models disorder-induced local force-constant variations.
The proposed framework explicitly models anharmonic effects.
The framework will be calibrated against first-principles calculations and experimental phonon data.
Chemical disorder induces local force-constant fluctuations in HEAs.
Force-constant fluctuations scatter acoustic phonons and affect their attenuation and lifetimes.
Random interatomic-force variations reduce phonon lifetimes and thereby contribute to low lattice thermal conductivity.
Anharmonic effects accompany the force-constant disorder and contribute to phonon scattering in the targeted HEAs.
Conventional DFT-based and empirical approaches generally overlook or oversimplify disorder-induced force-constant fluctuations.
Inadequate treatment of force-constant fluctuations causes conventional approaches to overestimate phonon lifetimes.
Inadequate treatment of force-constant fluctuations causes conventional approaches to overestimate lattice thermal conductivity.
For HEAs with moderate compositional disorder, the proposed framework will reduce thermal-conductivity predictive error by at least a factor of two relative to conventional approaches.
The framework's accuracy advantage will be confined primarily to nearly equiatomic HEAs whose constituent elements have similar atomic sizes and masses.
The framework's predictive advantage will diminish in HEAs with high atomic disparity because additional disorder sources become significant.
HCP or BCC HEAs with strong mass and size differences are examples for which the improvement may be minimal or absent.
Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering can characterize acoustic-phonon dispersions, attenuation, lifetimes, or linewidths in FeCoCrMnNi.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant two-fold reduction in predictive error for moderately disordered HEAs would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of the predictive advantage to diminish in high-atomic-disparity alloys would falsify the proposed applicability boundary.
